findings.message: Line carries two distinct normative obligations under a single @prd: PRD.01.09.d101 tag: (1) 'THE Visit Counter SHALL increment that code's visit count by exactly one … WITHIN the visit-count reconciliation window' (the count-delta + timing obligation) and (2) 'Each confirmed redirect event SHALL increment the counter exactly once; duplicate delivery of the same event SHALL NOT produce a second increment' (an exactly-once / idempotency obligation). These are independently testable rules (increment-by-one vs. dedup-on-duplicate-delivery) and should each be a separate atomic line with its own @prd tag. The iteration-1 splits (e8a5→ac68+9903, 8650→6811+4400) verified atomic, but did not cover this line, which remains conjoined.
findings.recommendation: Split into two lines, both tagged @prd: PRD.01.09.d101: line A keeps the WHEN-served increment-by-exactly-one obligation with the reconciliation-window WITHIN; line B states the event-driven exactly-once / no-double-increment obligation (deduplication mechanism owned by the visit-observability ADR topic, BRD.01.08.c478). Retain the cross-reference to EARS.01.03.f766 for the concurrent-no-loss counterpart.

findings.message: Primary obligation (return a unique short code that resolves to the exact submitted URL WITHIN the create-path screening deadline) is atomic, but the line also carries a trailing normative sentence ('A duplicate submission … MAY return … either outcome SHALL satisfy the code-to-URL uniqueness invariant (EARS.01.03.bca8)'). Because that clause explicitly defers ownership to the ubiquitous uniqueness rule bca8, it reads as a consistency restatement rather than an independent obligation — a minor atomicity smell, not a true conjoined rule — but the embedded SHALL slightly muddies the single-rule-per-line boundary.
findings.recommendation: Optional: demote the duplicate-submission sentence to a non-normative note (e.g., 'Note: a duplicate submission may reuse or reissue a code; uniqueness is owned by EARS.01.03.bca8') so the line carries exactly one SHALL obligation. No new @prd tag required since bca8 already owns the invariant.
